papers.title: EINN: An enzyme-informed neural network guided by an enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic model.
papers.abstract: Predicting cellular metabolism from molecular data is a central challenge in systems biology, with direct implications for engineering microbial cell factories. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) provide a mechanistic foundation for such predictions, but their accuracy is limited by an inability to account for the finite catalytic capacity of the proteome. Enzyme-constrained GEMs (ecGEMs) address this by incorporating enzyme turnover numbers and proteome allocation constraints. Hybrid neural-mechanistic models like Artificial Metabolic Network (AMN) and Metabolic-Informed Neural Network (MIN
papers.summary: This paper introduces EINN, a neural network architecture that integrates enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models to predict cellular metabolism more accurately. By incorporating enzyme kinetic and proteome allocation constraints, EINN improves metabolic predictions compared to standard approaches, offering a promising tool for engineering microbial cell factories.

papers.title: Strategies and applications for alleviating carbon catabolite repression.
papers.abstract: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) is a widespread regulatory strategy across diverse microorganisms that prioritises the utilisation of preferred carbon sources. In industrial bioprocesses, however, CCR-mediated substrate hierarchy can delay the utilisation of secondary carbon sources in mixed feedstock, thereby extending fermentation time and limiting carbon conversion efficiency toward target products. Existing reviews have largely addressed CCR in a microorganism-specific manner, potentially obscuring conserved principles, limiting cross-species comparisons, and constraining generalisable
papers.summary: This review discusses carbon catabolite repression (CCR), a regulatory mechanism in microbes that prioritizes certain carbon sources, which can hinder industrial bioprocesses by delaying the use of secondary substrates. The authors propose that existing reviews are too microorganism-specific and aim to identify conserved principles and generalizable strategies to alleviate CCR for improved fermentation efficiency.

papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new method that aligns consecutive tissue sections imaged with different spatial omics technologies using only the tissue images, without needing shared molecular features or annotations. It achieves alignment accuracy comparable to existing uni-modal tools across various tissues and resolutions, enabling the creation of unified multi-modal molecular datasets for downstream analysis.

papers.title: Single-cell multimodal analysis reveals enhancer and transcription factor regulatory dynamics during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation.
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes are widely used to model cardiac development and disease, but directed differentiation produces heterogeneous cellular states whose regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Here, we used simultaneous high-throughput ATAC and RNA Expression with sequencing (SHARE-seq) to profile gene expression and chromatin accessibility during human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte differentiation. Weighted nearest neighbor integration resolved sequential developmental cell states, including iPSCs, mesodermal cells, progenitor populations,
papers.summary: This study uses SHARE-seq to simultaneously profile chromatin accessibility and gene expression during human iPSC-to-cardiomyocyte differentiation, revealing sequential developmental states and the enhancer and transcription factor regulatory dynamics that drive cardiomyocyte maturation. The findings provide a high-resolution multimodal map of cardiac differentiation, highlighting key regulatory networks that could improve differentiation protocols and disease modeling.

papers.title: Deciphering the Mechanisms of Statin-Ezetimibe Drug Combinations Using Boolean Logical Modeling and Transcriptomic Data.
papers.abstract: Drug Combinations offer increased therapeutic efficacy and reduced toxicity compared with single agents. Understanding a drug combination's mechanisms of action (MoA) can provide important insights into therapeutic efficacy. The MoA of many FDA-approved drugs, however, often remains unclear. To decipher the underlying molecular mechanisms of drugs used alone and in combination, we investigated the combination of a statin (atorvastatin or simvastatin) plus ezetimibe using drug-treated RNA-seq transcriptome data from the human hepatocyte-like SOAT2-only-HepG2 cells and from liver biopsies of non
papers.summary: This study uses Boolean logical modeling combined with transcriptomic data to decipher the mechanisms of action of statin-ezetimibe drug combinations, revealing how these drugs work together at a molecular level. The approach provides a framework for understanding the synergistic effects of drug combinations, which could inform more effective therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: System level identification and multidimensional analysis of hub genes reveal complex regulatory networks underlying human iPSC differentiation into motor neurons.
papers.abstract: Human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) hold considerable potential for generating motor neurons (MNs), offering new avenues for disease modeling and regenerative medicine. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying iPSC differentiation into MNs, we conducted an integrated bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from the mature Day 28 stage of a publicly available 28-day iPSC differentiation dataset. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using STRING and visualized in Cytoscape, while CytoHubba identified 15 hub genes, including BUB1, TOP2A, AURKB, CCNA2
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from human iPSC differentiation into motor neurons to identify 15 hub genes and construct protein-protein interaction networks, revealing complex regulatory networks underlying the differentiation process. The findings provide candidate genes and pathways that may inform disease modeling and regenerative medicine applications.

papers.title: Cross-Species Transcriptomic and Network Analysis of Human and Canine Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Identifies a Conserved Replication-DNA Damage Module for Drug Repurposing.
papers.abstract: Rational, mechanism-based drug selection for canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains limited, despite extensive molecular work in human DLBCL. We asked whether human and canine DLBCL share a conserved transcriptional network that could anchor therapeutic hypotheses for dogs. Using public human and canine DLBCL transcriptomes, we derived a 409-gene cross-species module defined by concordant tumour-normal dysregulation and projected it onto pathway and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks. The module was dominated by DNA replication, cell-cycle checkpoint and DNA damage-respon
papers.summary: This study identifies a conserved 409-gene transcriptional module shared between human and canine diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, dominated by DNA replication and DNA damage response pathways. The module was used to propose drug repurposing opportunities for canine DLBCL, providing a mechanism-based approach to therapy selection in dogs.

papers.title: A Scoping Review of Male Fertility Assessment and Treatment Across Historical and Contemporary Paradigms.
papers.abstract: Male factor infertility accounts for up to 50% of couples' inability to conceive. Despite this significant burden, perspectives on male fertility have evolved over millennia, shaped by cultural, medical, and scientific frameworks. Tracing this trajectory illuminates how historical observations laid the foundations for modern andrological science.
papers.summary: This review traces the historical evolution of male fertility assessment and treatment, from ancient cultural beliefs to modern andrological science, highlighting how past observations have shaped current clinical practices. It underscores the persistent burden of male factor infertility, which accounts for up to half of conception difficulties, and calls for integrating historical context into contemporary approaches.

papers.title: Green tea-mediated modulation of body weight gain: roles of sex, diet, and housing temperature.
papers.abstract: Green tea (GT) is widely recognized for its metabolic effects, but the influence of biological sex and housing temperature on its response during diet-induced obesity remains incompletely understood. Male and female C57BL/6 mice were housed at standard temperature (22 °C) or thermoneutrality (28 °C), fed a standard diet (SD) or high-fat diet (HFD), and, after obesity induction, received GT by oral gavage at 500 mg/kg, five days per week, for 12 weeks. Longitudinal mixed-effects modeling and endpoint factorial ANCOVA showed that GT attenuated HFD-associated body weight gain in both sexes and at
papers.summary: This study investigates how sex and housing temperature influence the metabolic effects of green tea (GT) in a mouse model of diet-induced obesity. The findings show that GT reduces high-fat diet-associated weight gain in both sexes and at different temperatures, but the magnitude of the effect is modulated by these factors. The work highlights the importance of considering biological and environmental variables in preclinical studies of dietary interventions.

papers.title: A pan-tissue multi-omics resource atlas of coordinated immune, metabolic, and fibrotic alterations in diet-induced MASH.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a systemic metabolic disease involving coordinated alterations across multiple organs. Here, we established a diet-induced murine model of MASH and performed integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic profiling across seven metabolic tissues and the circulation, encompassing the liver, white and brown adipose tissues, skeletal muscle, gallbladder, pancreas, and plasma. Multi-omics analyses identified coordinated molecular changes across tissues, including altered immune, metabolic, and fibrotic programs. Metabolomic profilin
papers.summary: This study presents a comprehensive multi-omics resource atlas of diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in mice, integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data across seven metabolic tissues and plasma. The findings reveal coordinated immune, metabolic, and fibrotic alterations across organs, providing a valuable reference for understanding the systemic nature of MASH.

papers.title: Sustained improvement in renal function with palopegteriparatide in adults with chronic hypoparathyroidism: 2-year results from the phase 3 PaTHway-trial.
papers.abstract: The PaTHway clinical trial demonstrated sustained efficacy, safety, and tolerability of daily palopegteriparatide in the treatment of adults with hypoparathyroidism. Palopegteriparatide treatment was also associated with improvements in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over 52 wk in a post hoc analysis, prompting further exploration of palopegteriparatide in the preservation of renal function. The current post hoc analysis evaluated the impact of palopegteriparatide treatment on renal function in adults with hypoparathyroidism through Week 104; as with prior analysis, changes in ren
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
papers.summary: This post hoc analysis of the phase 3 PaTHway trial shows that 2 years of palopegteriparatide treatment in adults with chronic hypoparathyroidism is associated with sustained improvement in renal function, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). The findings support the potential of palopegteriparatide to preserve or improve kidney health in this patient population.

papers.title: Latent gene network expression underlies partial re-evolution of a polyphenic trait in the worker caste of ants.
papers.abstract: Polyphenisms-where alternative phenotypes develop from a single genome in response to environmental cues-are not only widespread in nature, but also occur at multiple levels of biological organization, from cells to individuals to societies. Polyphenism is thought to promote phenotypic diversification through the gain, loss, and re-evolution of alternative phenotypes. After the origin of a polyphenism, one of the alternative phenotypes often retains the developmental capacity to produce the ancestral trait, thereby permitting the other to evolve rapidly. Yet, little is known about the developm
papers.summary: This study investigates the developmental mechanisms underlying the partial re-evolution of a polyphenic trait in ant worker castes, revealing that latent gene network expression enables the re-emergence of an ancestral phenotype. The findings provide insights into how polyphenisms can promote phenotypic diversification through the gain, loss, and re-evolution of alternative phenotypes.

papers.title: Canon enables causal inference of downstream genes in single-cell CRISPR studies via instrumental variable analysis.
papers.abstract: A critical analytical task in sc-CRISPR screening is identifying downstream genes influenced by perturbed target genes. Existing methods for this task primarily rely on traditional association-based analyses, which not only fall short in establishing causal relationships between genes but also suffer from high false positive rates and limited statistical power. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a causal inference-based framework that leverages the perturbation status of gRNAs in single cells as instrumental variables (IVs) to infer causal gene relationship via IV analysis. Building u
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This paper introduces Canon, a causal inference framework for single-cell CRISPR screens that uses guide RNA perturbation status as instrumental variables to identify downstream genes causally affected by target gene perturbations. Unlike traditional association-based methods, Canon reduces false positives and improves statistical power by establishing causal rather than merely correlational gene relationships.

papers.title: Robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication modulates cell fate decisions by relaying information across tissues and inducing intracellular responses mediated by gene regulatory networks. Although the inference of cell-cell communication from high-throughput data is gaining popularity, studying how communication pathways operate across biological scales and influence cell fate decisions remains challenging. Here, we present scRICH (robust identification of cell-cell communication heterogeneity in single cells), a computational framework that leverages single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to unravel the he
papers.summary: This paper presents scRICH, a computational framework that uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data to identify heterogeneity in cell-cell communication across biological scales. It aims to reveal how communication pathways influence cell fate decisions, addressing a key challenge in the field.

papers.title: Mitochondrial-Centered Biological Networks in Metabolic Disease: Toward Precision Mitochondrial Medicine.
papers.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are multifactorial metabolic disorders characterized by progressive dysfunction of multiple organs and biological systems. Although mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of disease progression, the mechanisms linking metabolic stress to coordinated tissue dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Comparative proteomic studies have consistently identified coordinated remodeling of oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid oxidation, tricarboxylic acid cycle activity, redox regulation, mitochondrial proteostasis, and adaptive signaling across metabolically affec
papers.summary: This review discusses how mitochondrial dysfunction contributes to obesity and type 2 diabetes, highlighting coordinated changes in multiple mitochondrial pathways across tissues. It proposes a 'precision mitochondrial medicine' approach that uses mitochondrial-centered biological networks to better understand and treat metabolic diseases.

papers.title: IAN, an intelligent system for omics data analysis and discovery.
papers.abstract: IAN is an R package addressing the challenge of integrating, analyzing, and interpreting gene expression data using an artificial intelligence (AI) system. It leverages popular pathway (KEGG, WikiPathways, Reactome, and GO) and regulatory datasets (ChEA), along with STRING for protein-protein interactions, to perform standard enrichment analysis. A multi-agent architecture uses individual enrichment results to generate summaries using large language models (LLMs). These summaries are contextually integrated and interpreted by the LLM, guided by engineered prompts and grounding instructions, to
papers.summary: IAN is an R package that integrates gene expression data analysis with AI, using multi-agent LLM architecture to summarize and interpret enrichment results from multiple pathway and regulatory databases. It provides context-aware, grounded interpretations to aid biological discovery.

papers.title: IAGRN: An Interleaved-Attention Graph Neural Network for Gene Regulatory Network Inference.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) describe regulatory interactions between transcription factors and their target genes and are essential for understanding cellular processes and disease mechanisms. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) have enabled data-driven GRN inference at single-cell resolution. However, the high sparsity and noise inherent in scRNA-seq data pose substantial challenges for accurately recovering regulatory relationships. Existing graph neural network (GNN)-based approaches often rely on localized message passing, which can lead to over-smoothing and limi
papers.summary: This paper introduces IAGRN, a graph neural network with an interleaved-attention mechanism designed to infer gene regulatory networks from single-cell RNA sequencing data. The method addresses challenges of data sparsity and noise by improving long-range dependency capture and reducing over-smoothing compared to existing GNN approaches.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis of Multiple Sclerosis Reveals Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Landscapes and Discordant Methylation-Expression Coupling.
papers.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated central nervous system disease with mapped genetic risk loci but unresolved cross-layer regulatory mechanisms. We harmonised 30 primary public MS datasets spanning bulk transcriptomics (552 samples, 367 MS/185 healthy control [HC]), DNA methylation arrays (475 samples, 244 MS/231 HC) with sorted-cell whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) assessment, single-cell RNA sequencing (RNA-seq; 517,533 cells from 81 donors), and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and brain white-matter proteomes, and UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UK Biobank-PPP) plasma pr
papers.summary: This study integrates 30 public multi-omics datasets—including bulk transcriptomics, DNA methylation, single-cell RNA-seq, and proteomics—to map cell-type-specific regulatory changes in multiple sclerosis (MS). The authors identify discordant methylation-expression coupling across cell types and highlight specific regulatory landscapes that may underlie MS risk loci, providing a more integrated view of disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanism of Cinnamaldehyde Intervening in Ochratoxin A-Induced Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Comorbidity: An Integrated Approach Based on Network Pharmacology, Network Toxicology and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Cinnamaldehyde (CA) is a naturally occurring bioactive compound derived from the leaves, bark, roots, and flowers of the Chinese medicinal plant Cinnamomum cassia. It exhibits a broad spectrum of pharmacological properties, encompassing antioxidant, antibacterial, anti-diabetic, antifungal, and anticancer activities. Notably, it has shown potential therapeutic benefits in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Ochratoxin A (OTA), a common contaminant found in foods such as cereals, coffee, and raisins, is also pres
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, network toxicology, and molecular docking to explore how cinnamaldehyde (CA) may counteract the effects of ochratoxin A (OTA), a food contaminant linked to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). The findings suggest that CA may modulate key molecular targets and pathways involved in these comorbid conditions, providing a theoretical basis for its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Alzheimer's Disease as a Multi-Layer Network Disorder: A Systems Biology Framework Integrating Multi-Omics Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial progress in biomarker discovery and multi-omics profiling, several features of Alzheimer's disease (AD), including prolonged compensated states, heterogeneous clinical trajectories, and marked stage-dependent therapeutic responses, remain difficult to integrate into a single mechanistic framework. In this review, we propose an integrative and testable conceptual framework that reframes AD as a single, progressive multi-layer network disorder whose dynamics arise from hierarchical constraint propagation and progressive loss of cross-scale coordination. Integrating evidence f
papers.summary: This review proposes a new conceptual framework for Alzheimer's disease (AD) as a multi-layer network disorder, integrating multi-omics data to explain its complex features like prolonged compensated states and heterogeneous trajectories. It suggests that AD progression arises from hierarchical constraint propagation and loss of cross-scale coordination, offering a testable model to unify diverse mechanistic evidence.

papers.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.
papers.summary: This review examines the role of TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease, highlighting how macrophage heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity beyond the traditional M1/M2 paradigm contribute to disease pathogenesis. It positions TREM2 as a key molecular hub in immune-metabolic crosstalk and discusses the therapeutic potential of targeting TREM2 in cardiovascular contexts.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome, particularly Fusobacterium nucleatum, modulates tumor metabolism and drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model, trained on thousands of drug combination profiles, identifies synergistic therapies that account for microbial influences, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware cancer treatment design.

papers.title: Integrative machine learning and single-nucleus transcriptomics reveal MAPK-centered neuronal responses underlying the potential Alzheimer's disease risk of GenX.
papers.abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide-dimer acid (GenX or HFPO-DA) is a novel per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance developed as a replacement for legacy compounds, yet its potential neurotoxic effects remain poorly understood. In this study, we combined bibliometric profiling, in silico target prediction, in vivo behavioral assessments, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), network biology, machine learning, molecular docking, and in vitro validation to explore the potential relevance of GenX in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Bibliometric analysis revealed increasing research attention to GenX-associated he
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple approaches, including single-nucleus transcriptomics and machine learning, to investigate the neurotoxic effects of the PFAS replacement chemical GenX and its potential link to Alzheimer's disease. The findings point to MAPK-centered neuronal responses as a key mechanism, suggesting that GenX exposure may contribute to AD risk through this pathway.

papers.title: Longitudinal zone- and cell type-specific pattern-triggered immune responses in Arabidopsis roots.
papers.abstract: Roots, composed of diverse cell types across longitudinal developmental zones, are vital for plant survival against microbial challenges. Leveraging single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging of Arabidopsis roots, we reveal here that plant-derived phytocytokines elicit more potent immune responses than microbe-derived patterns across root cell types and zones. The differential expression of receptors and key signaling modules in distinct cell types and zones contributes to the response intensity to specific elicitors. Phytocytokines sustain growth-defense trade-offs by suppressing the e
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics and live-cell imaging to map pattern-triggered immune responses across cell types and developmental zones in Arabidopsis roots. It finds that plant-derived phytocytokines induce stronger immune responses than microbe-derived patterns, with receptor expression and signaling modules shaping cell-type-specific response intensities. The work provides insights into how roots balance growth and defense.

papers.title: Deciphering cell state transitions by logical modeling with single-cell transcriptome data.
papers.abstract: Cell state transitions are essential for diverse cell fate decision processes. Such transitions are mostly irreversible in natural environments, but they can be reversed under certain conditions. This raises a question on the largely unknown regulatory mechanisms underlying the asymmetric cell state transitions in forward and backward directions. Here, we present scDECIPHER (single-cell dynamic explorer of complex interactions and pathway hierarchies), an integrative framework designed to address this question using single-cell resolution transcriptome data measured over cell state transitions
papers.summary: This paper introduces scDECIPHER, a computational framework that uses logical modeling of single-cell transcriptome data to decipher the regulatory mechanisms underlying cell state transitions, particularly focusing on why these transitions are often irreversible in nature but can be reversed under certain conditions. The framework aims to uncover the asymmetric regulatory logic governing forward and backward transitions.

papers.title: CRITERIA: A network decomposition and elementary flux mode translation-based tool for computing equilibria of biochemical systems.
papers.abstract: Analytically deriving equilibria, which often govern the long-term behavior of biochemical reaction networks, is essential for understanding cellular decision-making and robustness, yet remains computationally challenging for large and complex systems. The COMPILES framework of Hernandez et al. addresses this problem via network decomposition but is limited by a computationally intensive translation step and by its restriction to networks with zero kinetic deficiency. We introduce CRITERIA (Computing paRametrized posITive EquilibRIA), a new framework that overcomes these limitations through tw
papers.summary: CRITERIA is a new computational tool that efficiently computes equilibria of biochemical reaction networks by decomposing the network and translating elementary flux modes, overcoming limitations of the previous COMPILES framework such as computational intensity and restriction to zero kinetic deficiency. This enables analysis of larger and more complex systems, aiding understanding of cellular decision-making and robustness.

papers.title: Assessment of gut microbiota dynamics and probiotic impact on HPV-associated head and neck cancer using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major etiological factor in head and neck cancers, primarily through the oncogenic activities of viral proteins E6 and E7, which disrupt the p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) tumor suppressor pathways. This disruption promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation, immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation, and malignant transformation. Although probiotics have emerged as promising modulators of the microbiome and host immune responses, their mechanistic role in HPV-associated head and neck cancer remains insufficiently understood. Therefore, this study investigated the th
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how gut microbiota composition and probiotic supplementation influence immune responses in HPV-associated head and neck cancer, using 16S rRNA sequencing and cytokine profiling. The findings suggest that probiotics may modulate gut microbial dynamics and systemic inflammation, offering a potential adjunctive strategy for managing this cancer type.

papers.title: Uncovering the molecular landscape of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer: A relieff-based feature selection analysis on RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Diffuse Gastric Cancer (DGC) is an aggressive subtype with a poor prognosis and a lack of specific biomarkers, representing a critical unmet need in oncology. This study aimed to elucidate the key molecular drivers of DGC by integrating RNA-seq data with a multi-faceted bioinformatics approach.
papers.summary: This study uses RNA-seq data and a ReliefF-based feature selection method to identify key molecular drivers of young-onset diffuse gastric cancer, a subtype with poor prognosis and few biomarkers. The analysis reveals potential gene signatures and pathways that may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for this aggressive cancer.
